summary: Translate the singular possessive šaġolayḏi as “My worker”.
rationale: The Turoyo has u šaġolayḏi, with the first-person singular possessive -ayḏi, followed by ono (I). Our changes the possessor to first-person plural. The same suffix in this batch appears in u=abr-ayḏi (my son) and iḏi (my hand).

summary: File mgawliwa under Infectum-wa rather than Preterit.
rationale: The target verb mgawliwa is a plural Infectum with -wa, coordinated with gmaḥtiwa and saymiwayle in a description of habitual building practice. The supplied corpus and translation confirm repeated past activity, not a -le preterit.

summary: Move the recording citation and repeated line marker out of the Turoyo field.
rationale: The trailing parenthesized recording identifier is provenance, followed by the repeated 060: marker introducing the English line in raw. Neither is part of the Turoyo utterance. The supplied old-houses text contains the quoted utterance without this tail. Preserve the recording identifier in refs.

summary: Correct the malformed English clause about lumps.
before: They are resulted in this way lumps
after: They became lumps in this way
rationale: Are resulted cannot form a passive of result, and the clause also lacks a grammatical complement construction. Howewa hawxa falqe is translated in the supplied corpus as Like so they became clumps; became lumps repairs the existing clause without changing its meaning.
